_comment: Dynamic tools configuration for Klawed Browser Controller.
_description: Copy or symlink this to .klawed/dynamic_tools.json, or set KLAWED_DYNAMIC_TOOLS env var.
_setup: Install the Chrome extension + Go host first: cd chrome_extension_native_messaging/host && make install EXTENSION_ID=<your-id>

function.name: BrowserControl
function.description:
Control a real Chrome/Chromium browser via the Klawed Browser Controller extension (must be connected - green dot in toolbar).

WINDOW ISOLATION — windowId is MANDATORY: Every command that targets a page, DOM element, or tab MUST include a windowId in params. The only exceptions are: newWindow (returns windowId), listWindows, ping, and getInfo. Call newWindow() first — it returns {windowId: N}. Then pass {windowId: N} in every subsequent command. Commands without windowId are REJECTED with an error. This eliminates any possibility of agents colliding on the same window.

ALERT HANDLING: All JavaScript dialogs (alert, confirm, prompt, beforeunload) are auto-detected via Chrome DevTools Protocol and auto-accepted. Dialog details appear in a "_alerts" field on the next command response: an array of {type, message, url} objects. Check this field on every command result — it tells you what dialogs were dismissed on your window/tab.

ALWAYS prefer evaluate() over structured commands — it's faster, more reliable, bypasses CSP everywhere, and gives you full JS power. Structured commands are convenience wrappers; use them when they're simpler, but reach for evaluate() whenever you need precision, complex state access, or shadow DOM.

PRIMARY — evaluate(code): execute arbitrary JS via CDP Runtime.evaluate. This is your main tool for reading, clicking, typing, scrolling, form-filling — everything. It bypasses CSP on any page (SPAs, strict headers, all work). Note: first evaluate call attaches the Chrome debugger, which shows a "debugging this browser" warning bar — this is normal and auto-detaches on navigation.

Windows:    newWindow(url?) — creates a fresh Chrome window, returns windowId; closeWindow(windowId); listWindows — list all windows with IDs and tabs
Navigation:  navigate(url), goBack, goForward, reload, newTab(url), closeTab(tabId), switchTab(tabId)
Tab info:    listTabs, getActiveTab
Read:        getText(selector?, maxLength?), getReadableText(maxLength?), getPageSource(maxLength?) — scripts/styles stripped; default 20k chars
DOM:         click(selector), type(selector,text,clearFirst?) — types with human-like delays (50-200ms per char) to evade bot detection —, getHtml(selector?), getAttribute(selector,attribute)
             findElements(selector,limit?=50), getLinks(limit?=50), getForms, fillForm(data) — fills instantly; use type() instead when bot detection matters —, submitForm(selector?), pressKey(selector?,key), uploadFile(selector, filePaths)
Scroll:      scroll(x,y), scrollBy(dx,dy), scrollToElement(selector)
Wait:        waitForElement(selector,timeout?)
Capture:     screenshot
Debug:       ping, getInfo

Code is king — evaluate() gives you direct JS access to the page. Use it for: reading page state (document.title, window.location, localStorage), clicking (document.querySelector('...').click()), scrolling (window.scrollTo(0,500)), waiting (new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 2000))), DOM traversal, and anything structured commands can't handle. IMPORTANT: For typing/text-entry into form fields, prefer the type() command over evaluate() — it types with human-like delays to avoid bot detection. fillForm() sets fields instantly (bot-like); use type() when anti-bot measures are likely.

Tip: use evaluate() for everything; use getText/getReadableText when you just need a quick page text extract; use getPageSource sparingly — it's heavy.

params.description: Command parameters. windowId is MANDATORY for all commands except newWindow/listWindows/ping/getInfo. E.g. {"windowId":42, "url":"https://..."}, {"windowId":42, "selector":"#id"}, {"windowId":42, "maxLength":4000}. Call newWindow first to get a windowId.
